newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar down on low demand, increased supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar down on low demand, increased supply.

text.p: Indian sugar ended Monday down on poor demand and improved supply, dealers said.
They said demand from consumers was low while supplies from mills were good.
In ready delivery, sugar S-30 fell 25 rupees to 1,390/1,430 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 lost 5 rupees to 1,440/1,480 rupees per quintal, dealers said.
They said the fall in the prices of S-30 sugar was higher compared to the M-30 varieties as mill production of M-30 was lower.
Sugar mill delivery fell to 1,345/1,355 rupees per quintal from 1,350/1,365 rupees.
Dealers said market sentiment was subdued at close as some traders were expecting the government to further increase the current month's quota of free sale sugar.
The government had hiked quota by 50,000 tonnes to 800,000 tonnes earlier in May.
